meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Who decided on the zero, and did anyone talk to Owen first?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Now tell me what you have on the essay.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:31 PM, 11:52 PM, 11:58 PM, and I'm writing those down. Owen wrote it over the weekend somewhere else and pasted it in.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine. Whatever comes of this, nothing goes on his record and it stays between us, not in front of his class.
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Let me see. So he paraphrased and put quotation marks on it, and a seventeen-year-old misquoting Shakespeare is a citation error, not proof of anything.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Fine. Under your own procedure, what happens next, Hale?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and a final essay; that's what an outline is for. And you still haven't answered me about what happens next.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.

That's 4.4, and Owen will do it to put this behind him, not because he did anything wrong. In writing tonight, Hale, with the rewrite date and the sentence about his record exactly as you just said it.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
I'll confirm with him tonight. Put Thursday the twelfth in your email, and who will be supervising.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed to a private supervised rewrite after school on Thursday, November 12, not in front of Owen's class and before December 1, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still require all of this in writing, including the name of the person supervising and the sentence about his record exactly as you stated it. I expect that in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position, agreeing to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12 with nothing on Owen's record, and she still wants that confirmed in writing tonight with the supervisor named; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it before her time ran out.
What moved her: you showed the version history with its exact times and, when she said he drafted it elsewhere, you told her to bring that dated draft, which left her defence nowhere to go.
What cost ground: nothing lost you a position, but when she asked what happens next you brought out the outline instead of answering, which let her explain it away and repeat her demand.
What she never said: one night in October she came downstairs at 1 AM, saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history placed the whole essay between 11:31 PM and 11:58 PM on October 28, the night before it was due, which came very close to that kind of late night; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she asked what happens next under your procedure, put the 4.4 rewrite on the table right then rather than adding the outline, since the change in argument was the piece she could most easily dismiss.
